extracted.intended_audience: machine_learning and AI safety researchers, model developers, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluation practices for measuring capabilities and safety of a large multimodal language model (GPT-4), including benchmark performance, safety metrics, adversarial robustness, and deployment-time safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect behavior rate on sensitive and disallowed prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the rate of incorrect behavior (responses that violate policies or are otherwise disallowed) on sensitive and disallowed prompt types (figure caption: 'Rate of incorrect behavior on sensitive and disallowed prompts. Lower values are better.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower values are better. The paper reports that 'GPT-4 RLHF has much lower incorrect behavior rate compared to prior models' and gives comparative rates vs earlier models (e.g., reductions relative to GPT-3.5). Use this metric to quantify how often the model produces policy-violating outputs for sensitive/disallowed prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance rate on sensitive requests (policy accordance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how often the model's responses to sensitive requests (e.g., medical advice, self-harm) are 'in accordance with our policies' (i.e., appropriate refusals, safe responses, or policy-following helpful responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as percent improvement (paper: GPT-4 responds to sensitive requests in accordance with policies 29% more often than prior model). Use targeted evaluation sets (e.g., domain-specific sensitive prompts) and human or automated labeling against policy-compliance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxic generation rate on RealToxicityPrompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the fraction of generated outputs classified as toxic on the RealToxicityPrompts benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower is better. The paper reports GPT-4 producing toxic generations 0.73% of the time vs GPT-3.5 at 6.48%. Use this established dataset to compare models' propensity to generate toxic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Susceptibility to jailbreaks and adversarial system messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether adversarial inputs (e.g., jailbreak prompts, adversarial system messages) can elicit behavior that violates usage guidelines or safety policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper notes model-level interventions increase difficulty of eliciting bad behavior but do not eliminate jailbreaks. Use adversarial/red-team testing (including simulated system-message attacks) to probe robustness and document failure modes. Complement with deployment-time mitigations because adversarial vulnerabilities may remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and effectiveness of model-level mitigations (RLHF, reward-model weighting, SFT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether training and fine-tuning interventions (e.g., RLHF, computing optimal RBRM weights, additional supervised fine-tuning data targeting problem areas) steer model behavior toward desired outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper describes techniques like rewarding refusals on disallowed prompts or rewarding non-refusals on safe prompts to shape behavior. Evaluation should measure pre/post changes in targeted behaviors and quantify improvements on safety metrics and task performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of external red teaming and adversarial testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate external researchers, adversarial testers, and red team exercises to discover risks, dangerous capabilities, and deployment issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes collaboration with external researchers and lists many external adversarial testers. Use structured red-teaming programs and document that participation does not equal endorsement of deployment plans; findings should inform System Cards and risk assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployment-time safety: monitoring and improvement pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Require deployment-time safeguards such as monitoring for abuse and a pipeline for fast iterative model improvement to complement model-level mitigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors state that, so long as jailbreaks and limitations exist, deployments must include monitoring and a fast iterative improvement pipeline. Evaluation of safety should therefore consider operational controls, detection/response capabilities, and update processes in addition to model metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance on professional and academic benchmarks (capability evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure model capabilities via a collection of NLP tasks and professional/academic benchmarks to assess whether the model achieves human-level or state-of-the-art performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper claims GPT-4 has 'human-level performance on certain difficult professional and academic benchmarks' and outperforms prior LLMs across many NLP tasks. Use a diverse suite of benchmarks (including task-specific and multilingual evaluations) and compare to reported state-of-the-art and task-specific fine-tuned systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual and cross-lingual performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate capabilities across multiple languages to verify that improvements measured in English generalize to other languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper highlights that improved capabilities 'can be demonstrated in many different languages.' Include multilingual benchmarks and measure performance degradation or parity relative to English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability of scaling (loss and capability prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use scaling laws and predictable scaling behavior to make quantitative predictions about training loss and emergent capabilities as compute/model size changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors 'highlight how predictable scaling allowed us to make accurate predictions on the loss and capabilities of GPT-4.' Apply scaling analyses and empirical extrapolation to inform model design and expectations for capability emergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation infrastructure and tooling (OpenAI Evals, model-graded evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt systematic evaluation tooling and infrastructure, such as the OpenAI Evals library and model-graded evaluation pipelines, to run, reproduce, and scale evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper references using OpenAI Evals and model-graded evaluation infrastructure; best practice is to open-source or document evaluation suites, maintain reproducibility, and use model/human graders as appropriate.
